One thing that really grinds my gears about weather apps is when they prioritize maritime warnings over others. Weather Underground is literally hiding a *WINTER STORM WARNING* underneath 3 warnings for people with boats. It's December, I am not about to sail Lake Superior. Be smart with your UI/UX

I live in a rural area where my carrier's connectivity is weird - my location jumps all over a 20 mile radius, so having my wildly inaccurate location and movement data secured does make me feel better. One of my weather apps once thought that I was in the middle of Lake Michigan.

Thanks for making everyone aware of the tools that are needed for meteorology. I was in the USCG in the 80s and assisted NOAA with weather buoys on the Great Lakes. All of these tools keep us informed and safe.

If you want to track conditions in and near the Great Lakes where you’re at outside of your standard weather map, check out GLOS’ seagull.app, or seagull.glos.org. Take care and stay safe out there! (Map wind layers generated with model data from NOAA’s Operational Forecast System)

When I was on Wind now called Freedom mobile it could not even connect to a tower I stood beside. It was so spotty & garbage. Yes there are dead zones here in SW ON. Its really bad if you live along 1 of the great lakes. The signal has been known to carry & go weee. Or you get roaming signal issues.

I grew up with a weather radio on top of our refrigerator. Most of the time, it just sat there doing nothing unless my dad wanted to check the weather on Lake Erie to see if he wanted to go fishing that weekend. When it went off, though, it was piercingly loud and informed us what was happening.

They seem to be failing on all their equipment maintenance. I live in Fort Erie. We have one weather station, in lake Erie at Port Colborne. It never worked in the winter, and hasn't worked for a couple years. I was assured by someone at ECC that we would get all necessary weather alerts.
